claimed_purpose.text: HaluMem is presented as an important benchmark for evaluating AI memory systems, with this issue representing the first independent evaluation outside the original team.
HaluMem is a benchmark for measuring hallucination and memory performance of different memory systems.
HaluMem includes a Memory Extraction task evaluated on a medium-difficulty split

mechanisms.text: Memory Extraction metrics: R (Recall), Weighted R, Target P (Target Memory Precision), Acc. (Memory Accuracy), FMR (False Memory Resistance), F1 (Memory Extraction F1-score). Higher is better for all except none noted as lower.

Human annotation covered over 50% of Halu-Medium by 8 annotators, scoring memory points and QA pairs on correctness, relevance, and consistency; reported accuracy 95.70%, relevance 9.58/10, consistency 9.45/10.

Each memory system has a dedicated adapter script (e.g., eval_memzero.py, eval_memos.py, eval_memobase.py, eval_zep.py, eval_supermemory.py) following a shared input/output contract for fair comparison
Per-item scores aggregate into an overall_score dict with six named sub-scores: memory_integrity, memory_accuracy, memory_extraction_f1, memory_update, question_answering, memory_type_accuracy.
Zep cannot be evaluated on memory extraction because its API does not support retrieving all memory points within a session; only memory update and QA tasks are reliably scored for Zep
QA evaluation covers six question types: Basic Fact Recall, Dynamic Update, Multi-hop Inference, Generalization & Application, Memory Conflict, Memory Boundary.
An LLM (configurable via OPENAI_MODEL, e.g. gpt-4o) is used as part of the evaluation pipeline, with temperature set to 0.0.
Each memory system adapter follows the same input/output contract so the downstream scorer can compare systems fairly.
The official grader/judge for HaluMem is GPT-4o, described as the HaluMem standard.
HaluMem includes a QA task scored by accuracy.

ledger.claim: HaluMem has two dataset splits: Halu-Medium (20 users, 30,073 dialogues, ~160k tokens avg context, 14,948 memory points, 3,467 QA pairs) and Halu-Long (20 users, 53,516 dialogues, ~1M tokens avg context, 14,948 memory points, 3,467 QA pairs).
ledger.quote: Halu-Medium: #Users 20, #Dialogues 30,073, Avg. Sessions/User 70, Avg. Context Length ~160k tokens, #Memory Points 14,948, #QA Pairs 3,467. Halu-Long: #Users 20, #Dialogues 53,516, Avg. Sessions/User 120, Avg. Context Length ~1M tokens, #Memory Points 14,948, #QA Pairs 3,467.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face at IAAR-Shanghai/HaluMem.
ledger.quote: The complete HaluMem dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/IAAR-Shanghai/HaluMem
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Human annotation covered over 50% of Halu-Medium by 8 annotators, scoring memory points and QA pairs on correctness, relevance, and consistency; results: Accuracy 95.70%, Relevance 9.58/10, Consistency 9.45/10.
ledger.quote: A team of 8 annotators manually reviewed over 50% of Halu-Medium, scoring each session's memory points and QA pairs on correctness, relevance, and consistency. Results demonstrate high data quality: Accuracy: 95.70%, Relevance: 9.58 / 10, Consistency: 9.45 / 10

ledger.claim: Dataset construction used a six-stage pipeline: Persona Construction (seeded from Persona Hub 1B+ personas, refined with GPT-4o), Life Skeleton Planning, Event Flow Generation, Session Summaries & Memory Points, Multi-turn Session Generation, Question Generation.
ledger.quote: The HaluMem dataset was built through a six-stage, carefully controlled pipeline that combines programmatic generation, LLM-assisted refinement, and human validation... Personas were initially generated via rule-based templates seeded from Persona Hub (1B+ personas) and then refined using GPT-4o

ledger.claim: Four evaluation tasks are implemented and run: Memory Integrity, Memory Accuracy, Memory Update, and Question Answering.

ledger.claim: Memory extraction F1 is the primary combined metric, computed as harmonic mean of precision (target_accuracy(all)) and recall (recall(all)).
ledger.quote:
eval_results["overall_score"]["memory_extraction_f1"] = compute_f1(
        precision=eval_results["overall_score"]["memory_accuracy"]["target_accuracy(all)"],
        recall=eval_results["overall_score"]["memory_integrity"]["recall(all)"]
    )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory update and QA grading uses a three- or four-way classification: Correct, Hallucination, Omission (plus Other for updates), returned by LLM-as-judge functions.
ledger.quote:
if item["memory_update_type"] not in ["Correct", "Hallucination", "Omission", "Other"]:
            item["is_valid"] = False
            continue
        ...if item["result_type"] not in ["Correct", "Hallucination", "Omission"]:
            item["is_valid"] = False
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Importance-weighted recall is computed for memory integrity, where each golden memory has an 'importance' scalar.
ledger.quote:
memory_integrity_weighted_scores += 0.5 * item["memory_integrity_score"] * item["importance"]
            memory_integrity_weighted_valid_num += item["importance"]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory points marked with is_updated reference original_memories that are missing from the dataset, affecting more than 70% of such memory points.
ledger.quote: Some memory points marked with is_updated have original_memories that cannot be found in the user's memory points. For example, the original memory: "Martin Mark is considering a career change due to health impacts from his current role." According to my statistics, this issue occurs in more than 70% of memory points.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The benchmark has three operation-level task types: QA (question_answering_records), memory extraction (memory_integrity_records + memory_accuracy_records), and memory update (memory_update_records).
